context: OpenStax Calculus Volume 1 §3.1: both equivalent difference quotient limits are given with a as interior point. A one-sided endpoint derivative and a generalized derivative are separate conventions.
editorial_note: OpenStax Calculus Volume 1 §3.1: both equivalent difference quotient limits are given with a as interior point. A one-sided endpoint derivative and a generalized derivative are separate conventions.
text: For real f defined on an open interval containing a, its derivative f'(a), when it exists as a finite real number, is the limit as h→0 of [f(a+h)−f(a)]/h. Equivalently it is the limit as x→a of [f(x)−f(a)]/(x−a).

text: For each real x, |x| equals x when x≥0 and equals −x when x<0; it is nonnegative and |x−y| gives the usual distance between real x and y.
